data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The nocturnal UHI is primarily a wind-speed modulation phenomenon; cities with lower regional wind speed exhibit larger gaps because reduced ventilation prevents heat dissipation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If wind speed alone does not explain the variance in nocturnal UHI across cities after normalizing for urban form and heat sources, it is not the single best modulator.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the thermal storage release rate is the dominant energy term and is independent of wind speed, wind speed modulation is a secondary effect.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Under clear, calm nights, the urban heat island intensity is governed by the efficiency of horizontal and vertical heat dissipation. Wind speed is the primary cross-city modulator: in cities with lower wind speed, sensible heat from both daytime storage release and anthropogenic sources is not ventilated, resulting in a stronger, more pronounced UHI. In cities with higher wind speed, mechanical turbulence mixes the warm urban air with cooler surroundings, decreasing the nocturnal gap.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
